主要内容: The February 2020 Manufacturing ISM® Report On Business® indicated that the U.S. manufacturing sector expanded at a slower rate, with the PMI® at 50.1%, down from 50.9% in January. The New Orders Index fell to 49.8%, down 2.2 percentage points from January's 52.0, indicating a contraction in new orders. The Production Index dropped to 50.3%, a 4-point decline from January's 54.3, marking two months of growth after five consecutive months of contraction. Supply chain disruptions limited production growth. The Employment Index rose slightly to 46.9%, showing a slower contraction rate compared to January. Three industries reported employment growth, while nine saw declines. The Supplier Deliveries Index rose to 57.3%, reaching its highest level since November 2018. Concerns about Asian supply chain reliability dominated panelist comments. The Inventories Index dropped to 46.5%, a 2.3-point decrease from January, indicating a ninth consecutive month of contraction. The Customers' Inventories Index fell to 41.8%, showing customers' inventory levels were considered too low for the 41st consecutive month. The Prices Index declined to 45.9%, reflecting a 7.4-point drop from January, driven by falling raw material prices. The report highlights the impact of the coronavirus on supply chains, particularly affecting industries reliant on Chinese imports. Companies report delays in production due to supply chain disruptions and a slowdown in new orders. Despite these challenges, some sectors, such as Machinery and Plastics & Rubber Products, continue to see strong sales. The PMI® reading suggests that the overall economy is growing at 2.1% annually, marking the 130th consecutive month of economic expansion. However, the manufacturing sector is experiencing a slowdown after five months of contraction.
